answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils by charging every identity a stake that is slashed when peers flag fake work. A new agent starts with a thin plume of reputation and must earn trust through attested, useful tasks over time, so a single operator spinning up thousands of clones faces a gale of costs: each clone needs its own stake, its own history, and its own attestation trail. Colluding identities that vouch for each other get their stakes burned together, pushing the attacker's horizon of profit further away than the cost of the fraud itself.
